anytime_margin.name: RGNA4
anytime_margin.schedule: cumulative crossing allowance after b observed bits A(b) = delta * (6 / pi_u^2) * sum_{j=1..b} 1/j^2, pi_u = 355/113 (a rational upper bound on pi), so A(b) < delta * (6/pi^2) * (pi^2/6) = delta for every b (Exact)
anytime_margin.boundary_rule: the frozen brute.seqmargin.boundary dynamic program (exact Fractions over the binomial(eps_bar) flip path, raise m(b) until the probability of a first crossing by bit b <= A(b)) with A(b) in place of delta*b/B; eps_bar 0.02, delta 0.01
anytime_margin.horizon_free: m(b) depends only on b, eps_bar and delta (no planned B); prefix-stable: the boundary computed to any length L agrees with the boundary to L' > L on 0..L (Exact by construction; tested)
anytime_margin.region: frozen brute.seqmargin.SeqMarginRegionSpace(4, boundary, k) with the anytime boundary; certificates = the frozen RGN rule (singleton support after burn-in 8)
anytime_margin.soundness_lemma: If the true machine has <= 4 states and the running flip count never exceeds m(b), the true machine survives and every certificate equals the noise-free reading (Exact; same lemma as v0.17.0 GNB). P(any crossing) <= sum of first-crossing probabilities <= lim A(b) < delta under iid flips with eps <= eps_bar (Exact). Written as docs/research/v0.19.0/ANYTIME_LEMMA_021.md before the study code.
anytime_margin.why: v0.18.0 Exact: the planned boundary spends delta*b/B, so a longer planned horizon raises early margins (#106). The anytime schedule spends most of delta on the first bits and needs no B.
